target.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting
target.body:
Related: #1000
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108435

## What Problem This Solves

The Windows Companion had two independent problems:

1. Compact numeric labels were culture-sensitive under `pt-PT` and other decimal-comma locales.
2. The Companion-owned setup path did not safely coordinate Gateway wizard ownership with current OpenClaw. The wizard could install or restart the daemon while the Setup Engine was also managing it, and Gateway reload behavior could interrupt the in-flight wizard.

## Ownership and Design

- The Companion remains the owner of WSL, systemd, Gateway lifecycle, Windows Node bootstrap, and setup progress.
- OpenClaw remains the owner of the native onboarding wizard.
- The Companion starts the wizard with `installDaemon=false`, temporarily suspends Gateway reload immediately before the first `wizard.start`, and restores the configured reload mode on success, failure, or cancellation.
- Restoration failure is primary while retaining the original wizard exception or cancellation as an inner error.
- Initial and reconnect wizard starts use the same payload.
- The Setup Engine candidate targets official OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.1`.

This is intentionally a stacked draft. The validated E2E used a paired OpenClaw protocol change that accepts and honors `installDaemon=false`; this Companion PR must not be treated as independently merge-ready until that OpenClaw contract is upstream or otherwise available in the selected release.

## Changes

- Use invariant culture at the three existing compact-number formatting boundaries.
- Update the Setup Engine LKG to `2026.7.2-beta.1`.
- Add wizard `installDaemon=false` projection for initial and reconnect starts.
- Suspend and restore `gateway.reload.mode` around the native wizard with fail-closed lifecycle handling.
- Include Windows Node bootstrap context in final setup progress.
- Add focused orchestration, cancellation, restoration, payload, and LKG tests.

## Validation

Validated on Companion head `8e6962cdcd889486121b0676623dc7912307e7f8`:

- Full repository build: passed.
- Setup Engine: `435/435` passed.
- Shared: `2787` passed, `31` expected gated skips, `0` failed.
- Tray: `1717/1717` passed.
- Focused reload lifecycle: `4/4` passed.
- Disposable WSL setup E2E: `16/16` passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Temporary local-package transfer hook: removed and absent from the final diff.
- Scoped `openclaw-autoreview` with Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high: zero findings; `patch is correct`; confidence `0.91`.

Paired OpenClaw proof package:

- Base commit: `a0d6cd724ab603ba8fbf9af8a59a09ce57eeca1c` plus the isolated five-file wizard/package correction.
- Package SHA-256: `7444C9567DBABB8EED1BA7FFE5F3B06BFE116EB1B8B0D65C7A243A4719436E78`.

Failed-first evidence retained:

- The first disposable-WSL run found a stale Gateway listener during restart preflight. The fixture handling was corrected before the final `16/16` run.
- Earlier review findings about suspension timing, reconnect payload parity, bootstrap progress, restoration coverage, and cancellation/restoration priority were accepted and fixed.
- A proposed extra restart triggered only by restoring `gateway.reload.mode=restart` was rejected: current OpenClaw docs identify `gateway.reload` and `gateway.remote` as reload exceptions. The Companion still performs its explicit post-wizard restart to apply wizard configuration.

## Scope

- No `/new` or session behavior changes.
- No permission, token, secret, model, memory, plugin, or agent-policy changes.
- No runtime installation or Gateway mutation was performed while validating this PR.
- No OpenClaw core changes are included in this Companion diff.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities: No.
- Secret or token handling changes: No.
- New network destination: No.
- Broader command authority: No.

## Review Status

- [x] Current-head source and tests reviewed.
- [x] Supported disposable-WSL setup path passed with the paired OpenClaw package.
- [x] Scoped Auto-review is clean.
- [ ] Paired OpenClaw `installDaemon=false` contract is available upstream/in the selected release.
- [ ] GitHub CI passes on this new head.
- [ ] Maintainer review completed.

## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Sanitized operator/agent decision record</summary>

- This work followed an extended operator/agent recovery and validation cycle rather than a quick version bump.
- The operator required the Companion and OpenClaw to remain separate products with explicit ownership: the Companion owns installation and service lifecycle; OpenClaw owns native onboarding.
- We rejected both keeping a stale core indefinitely and masking core lifecycle defects with sleeps, lease deletion, disabled E2E, or duplicated daemon ownership.
- Failed-first tests and review findings were preserved, triaged against current source/docs, fixed only when in scope, and rerun through full tests, disposable-WSL E2E, and scoped Auto-review.
- The PR remains draft because its successful E2E depends on the paired OpenClaw protocol change; that dependency is stated rather than hidden.

</details>

target.title: refactor(setup): route SetupSteps WSL quoting through WslShellQuoting
target.body:
## Summary

Migrates `SetupSteps.cs` off three divergent private `ShellEscape` helpers onto the shared `WslShellQuoting` contract (added in PR 2, #994), then deletes the duplicates. This is a net-negative dedup and is **behavior-preserving** — the generated WSL scripts are byte-identical.

The three deleted helpers had two different wrap semantics; each call site was audited individually and mapped by the semantics of the helper it used:

| Step class | Old `ShellEscape` semantics | Call sites | New helper |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `InstallCliStep` | escape-only (caller supplies its own `'...'`) | `BuildInstallCommand`: installUrl, trimmedVersion | `WslShellQuoting.EscapePosixSingleQuoteInner` |
| `ConfigureGatewayStep` | fully-wrapped standalone token | allowedCommandsJson, inline defaultPublicUrl, ExtraConfig value | `WslShellQuoting.QuotePosixSingleQuote` |
| `WindowsNodeBootstrapContextStep` | fully-wrapped standalone token | `RunOpenclawSetupAsync` workspaceArg; `BuildApplyScript` / `BuildRollbackScript` bash-assignment lines | `WslShellQuoting.QuotePosixSingleQuote` |

The dangerous inversion — a wrapped variant where the caller already supplies `'...'` (yielding `''x''`), or an escape-only variant on a standalone token (yielding an unquoted/splittable arg) — does not occur: only the two escape-only sites have caller-supplied outer quotes.

`WslShellQuoting` stays `internal`; it is reachable from `OpenClaw.SetupEngine` via the existing `InternalsVisibleTo("OpenClaw.SetupEngine")` in `OpenClaw.Shared.csproj`. Making it `public` would needlessly widen the Shared surface, so it was left internal per existing repo convention.

## Validation

- `./build.ps1` — all projects succeeded.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests` — 2864 passed / 31 skipped (WSL/device integration skips).
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests` — 1717 passed.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests` — 426 passed.
- E2E setup suite — not run (gated/slow, requires a real WSL host). This PR is quoting-in-setup-scripts, not `system.run`/MXC; no migrated site feeds `system.run`/exec, and `RunOpenclawSetupAsync` / apply / rollback still deliver scripts via `inputViaStdin: true`, so no MXC/exec-approval surface is touched.

## Real behavior proof

Characterization tests pin the generated command/script strings **byte-for-byte** for representative inputs containing an embedded single quote, proving the migration is output-identical:

- `curl … '…install'\''s.sh' … --version '2026.5.22'\''a'` — `InstallCli_BuildInstallCommand_EscapesSingleQuotesInUrlAndVersion` (pre-existing, escape-only variant).
- `openclaw config set gateway.custom.note 'a'\''b'` — `ConfigureGateway_QuotesExtraConfigValueWithEmbeddedSingleQuote` (new).
- `workspace='/home/o'\''brien/.openclaw/workspace'` — `WindowsNodeContext_BuildApplyScript_QuotesWorkspacePathWithEmbeddedSingleQuote` and `…RollbackScript…` (new).

## Architecture ledger

- `wsl-posix-quoting`: residue cleared, invariant/retirement updated to reflect the migration is complete.
- New `setup-shellescape-closed` row (`closed`, `source-shape`) guarded by `SetupStepsShellEscapeClosureTests.SetupSteps_DoesNotReintroduce_PrivateShellEscape` — fails CI if a local `ShellEscape` reappears in `SetupSteps.cs` (the behavioral `WslShellQuotingTests` can't catch a re-added local helper).
- Updated the "when you touch `SetupSteps.cs`" extraction guidance.
- `ArchitectureLedgerConsistencyTests` remains green.

## Reviews (adversarial, multi-model) — GO

- **Author multi-model review — 6 models, all GO, no blocking issues:** GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 (rubber-duck), then expanded to Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.3-Codex, Claude Sonnet 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol (code-review). Each independently re-derived all 13 call-site variant mappings and confirmed byte-identity, unchanged stdin/WSL delivery, correct `$$"""..."""` raw-string interpolation, and a correct/false-positive-free ledger guard regex. Gemini additionally injected a fake helper to prove the guard fires.
- **Coordinator independent dual review — GPT-5.5 + Claude Opus 4.8, both GO:** re-derived all 13 sites and confirmed correct escape-only vs wrapped mapping and byte-identity; no blocking issues.
- **One condition flagged by review (satisfied):** the new closure guard test file `tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/Architecture/SetupStepsShellEscapeClosureTests.cs` must ship with the PR so the ledger doesn't reference an absent guard — it is included in this PR.

target.title: feat(setup): offer native Windows and WSL gateway modes
target.body:
## Summary

- make native Windows the recommended onboarding path while preserving the existing WSL 2 and connect-existing choices
- install the native CLI into an app-owned LocalAppData prefix and run an isolated profile/Scheduled Task without changing a user's global CLI or default profile
- make native/WSL switching, rollback, repair, and uninstall ownership-aware so inactive or user-managed runtimes are preserved
- complete the gateway wizard without trying to launch a terminal UI, follow native wizard logs across partial writes/rotation, and document both runtime modes

Builds on the onboarding redesign from #925.

## Verification

- Windows 11 ARM64 VM: full Release solution rebuild, 0 warnings / 0 errors
- SetupEngine: 553 passed
- Shared: 2,703 passed, 31 skipped
- Tray: 1,596 passed
- Connection: 399 passed
- WinNode CLI: 126 passed
- Functional UI: 10 passed
- WinUI: 78 passed on ARM64
- ARM64 self-contained publish plus release native-dependency policy: passed
- fresh native E2E: official CLI install, random isolated profile/port, HTTP 200 health, operator/node pairing, gateway wizard completion, tray ready, and clean uninstall
- post-uninstall probe: isolated profile/task absent; pre-existing global CLI path and `2026.6.11` version unchanged
- structured autoreview: clean

The Parallels validation VM can run WSL 1 but cannot provide the nested virtualization required for WSL 2, so a fresh WSL 2 provisioning run is not claimed here. The WSL choice/review path and runtime-selection/switching behavior remain covered by the setup test suite and existing CI E2E lane.

## Native setup reliability & WSL-parity follow-up (bc0077e4)

Follow-up pass to make native Windows setup as fast, deterministic, and non-blocking as the WSL path, without weakening its Windows-specific repair semantics:

- **Wizard** — give note/acknowledge steps the slow timeout ceiling so the finalize "Security" note ack survives the gateway's shell-completion work instead of timing out and stranding setup on the disclaimer screen.
- **Install** — skip the native CLI reinstall when the app-owned launcher already matches the pinned version (probes only the managed launcher; any mismatch or failure falls through to a full install).
- **Configure** — apply gateway config in one `config set --batch-file` instead of per-key CLI calls; the auth token stays in a temp file (never on argv), stale temp files are swept, and the file is always deleted in `finally`.
- **Start** — wait for the install-launched Scheduled Task via `/healthz` polling and fail terminal on timeout instead of issuing a destructive `gateway start`; verify ownership fail-closed on the identity signals the real `gateway status --json` reports (port, `Scheduled Task` label, `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, profile-state-dir `sourcePath`).
- **Installer** — apply the PowerShell 5 SQLite-probe quoting workaround only when the probe is present; otherwise proceed and surface a warning (the installer script is fetched live/unpinned).
- **Reinstall** — reset the app-owned native profile on clean runs to clear stale device/token state.
- **Perf** — sample CPU usage via `GetSystemTimes` instead of a synchronous `PerformanceCounter` first-touch that stalled post-setup node connect.
- Removed superseded device-token finalization helpers and past-approach comments.

### Validation (Debug, ARM64)

- `build.ps1`: all 5 projects, 0 warnings / 0 errors
- SetupEngine: 568 passed
- Shared: 2,732 passed, 31 skipped
- Tray: 1,681 passed
- Dual-model rubber-duck review (GPT-5.5 + Opus) plus a focused re-review of the fixes. The re-review caught a false-negative in the first ownership fix (it required `OPENCLAW_WINDOWS_TASK_NAME`, which the live status filters out of `service.command.environment`); corrected to the reliably-present identity signals and confirmed against a live managed gateway's `gateway status --json`.

Broader Release-matrix suites (Connection, WinNode CLI, WinUI, Functional UI, publish policy) and the fresh native E2E from the verification above are unaffected by this pass and were not re-run here; CI covers them.

target.title: test: stabilize build error persistence wait
target.body:
## Summary

- wait for the persisted build-error field, not merely for any state object
- keep timeout behavior so a missing persistence update still fails the existing assertions
- remove a race observed while validating the dependency queue

## Root cause

`initializeState()` makes `readState()` truthy before `updateBuildError()` finishes. The test helper returned on that initial state, so the fixed 50 ms delay sometimes left `lastBuildError` undefined. The helper now accepts a readiness predicate and waits for the field the test actually asserts.

## Proof

- Reproduced before the patch during the PR 180 full suite: `expected undefined to be defined` at `test/build-improvements.test.ts:217`.
- Focused test passed 15 consecutive stress runs after the patch. A later run under severe unrelated host CPU saturation timed out in a different test; the final normal focused run passed all 7 tests.
- `pnpm run build`: passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck`: passed.
- `pnpm run lint`: passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest --config vitest.config.ci.ts`: 113 files passed, 2 skipped; 702 tests passed, 31 skipped.
- `pnpm run build:bun:test`: built and executed both standalone binaries; both reported 2.1.2.
- `pnpm audit --audit-level high`: no known vulnerabilities.
- `~/.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; overall correctness 0.98.

Test-only change; no changelog entry.
